claimBoundary: This profile qualifies libjpeg-turbo classic-API input-suspension state handling as an independent progressive-JPEG mechanism probe. It does not qualify a production ImageCraft backend or make libjpeg-turbo a package dependency.

For every case, all chunk schedules must produce the same final RGB bytes, the same final scan count, the same scan-completed event sequence and the same implementation-observed consumed offsets; final RGB must also exactly match a one-shot djpeg decode using the same pinned libjpeg-turbo installation.

A separate marker parser independently establishes the structural SOS count. libjpeg scan-completion consumed offsets are retained as implementation observations and are not promoted to JPEG-format normative offsets.

The source work buffer is explicitly bounded. For the pinned libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 ABI only, the probe also observes jmemmgr total_space_allocated at lifecycle checkpoints and combines the EOI/final-render pool bytes with probe-owned source/output storage. These are source-bound allocator live-byte observations, not a stable libjpeg public API, cross-version promise or physical-RSS bound.

For the pinned 3.2.0 no-backing-store memory manager, the probe additionally models the virtual-array decision from pre-realize pool bytes, full coefficient-array maximum space, per-minheight access space and required minheight count. When more than one minheight is required, pre-realize pool plus full coefficient payload is a sharp falsifiable hinge: threshold-1 must fail with Memory limit exceeded before coefficient payload allocation, while the exact threshold must complete with identical RGB. When every array fits in the mandatory one-minheight fallback, the same 1-byte boundary is intentionally not claimed and a 1-byte configured limit must still complete exactly. Neither case makes max_memory_to_use a total-memory cap: row-pointer arrays, allocator headers/alignment and later allocations may raise total_space_allocated above the configured value after the virtual-array decision.
